tiers.label: Reach for first
tiers.blurb: The default answer. I have to be talked out of these, not into them.

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.note: Row-level security is the reason. Tenant isolation enforced in the database holds even when the application code above it is wrong — which is the only guarantee worth having.

tools.name: TypeScript
tools.note: Every project on this site is TypeScript end to end. The type boundary is where I catch content and API mistakes before they render.

tools.name: Next.js
tools.note: Server components by default, so a page that is really just content ships as content. This site runs on it.

tools.name: Node.js / Express
tools.note: The REST layer under most of what I build, including the lead pipeline platform in production at EPPS.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.note: Postgres with the auth and row-level-security plumbing already wired. It is what makes Orbit's multi-tenancy a schema decision rather than a backend project.

tiers.label: When the problem calls for it
tiers.blurb: Not defaults, but the right answer often enough to stay sharp on.

tools.name: SQLite
tools.note: Paired with Postgres in Commit behind one data-access layer, so local and production differ by a single line and environment drift never gets a foothold.

tools.name: Three.js
tools.note: The 3D bin-packing optimiser needed real spatial visualisation — container loads with door-clearance constraints are not a chart.

tools.name: D3
tools.note: Force-directed graphs in Orbit, where the shape of a network is the insight and a table would hide it.

tools.name: Gemini API
tools.note: Semantic search over a user's own connections in Orbit — retrieval where keyword matching genuinely fails.

tools.name: Stripe
tools.note: Free/Pro billing with usage metering in Orbit, with the metering function server-side so application code cannot drift from what was actually charged.

tools.name: Resend
tools.note: Daily digests in Commit, with a console fallback in development so a missing key never blocks local work.

tools.name: Nginx
tools.note: Reverse proxying and cache/hardening work across the 25+ domains and 7 production sites I keep running.

tools.name: Python
tools.note: Automation and scraping — catalogue sync via the Sheets API, reconnaissance tooling, reporting workflows. Rarely the product, often the thing that removes a weekly chore.

tiers.label: Security tooling
tiers.blurb: From the offensive-security internship. I use these to check my own work before someone else does.

tools.name: Burp Suite
tools.note: Intercepting my own traffic is the fastest way to find out what a client is really sending.

tools.name: OWASP Top 10
tools.note: The checklist I threat-model against before shipping, rather than the list I get audited on afterwards.

tiers.label: Worked with, not reaching for
tiers.blurb: Real production experience, but not where I would start a new system today. Listing them honestly is more useful than padding the section above.

tools.name: Java / Spring Boot
tools.note: Test-first REST APIs for a SaaS ERP at Kites, with Cucumber integration tests. Solid, and still my reference for how a typed backend should be structured.

tools.name: Django REST Framework
tools.note: Storefront APIs during freelance work — catalogues and enquiry forms for small businesses.

tools.name: Power BI
tools.note: Executive dashboards at EPPS, backing cost-benefit and ROI cases for software spend.

tools.name: WordPress / WooCommerce
tools.note: The e-commerce platform at HomeBay, plus the estate of sites I still keep patched and fast.
